title: How Your Kidneys Filter Blood

cues.text: Your kidneys are like a recycling plant that never stops.
The renal artery acts as the main delivery road, bringing raw, unfiltered blood directly from your heart.
Inside the kidney, over a million tiny machines called nephrons get to work.
Each one acts like a precise sieve, sorting what the body needs from what it must discard.
the nephron filters out waste but carefully reabsorbs water and nutrients, sending them back into your bloodstream.
Once the good stuff is reclaimed, the remaining waste and excess water become urine.
This liquid collects at the base of each nephron.
The ureter acts as a dedicated pipe, carrying this waste liquid away from the kidney to be stored for later disposal.
This constant flow ensures waste is moved efficiently out of your filtering plant and toward your storage tank.
The urine travels down to your bladder, which acts as a temporary storage tank.
It holds the waste until your body is ready to expel it.
When the tank is full, you feel the urge to go, and the waste is finally cleared from your body.
By constantly filtering and storing waste,
your kidneys ensure that only clean, balanced blood keeps circulating through your body.
